  "agentMessage": "Reading this as: a personal portfolio for engineering and applied-AI hiring teams, with an expressive editorial language built around “The working table.”\n\nI’m using the frontend-design skill: warm stone and chalk, a distinctive serif name paired with restrained sans-serif text, and three differently composed project studies. The keyboard material image will anchor the first screen; motion will stay limited to interaction feedback.The supplied image fits the direction: its exposed switch and stone texture give the page a tactile focal point. I’m pairing that with a large, offset serif name, a compact work index, and a graphite research spread.\n\nI’ll also use the AgentMemory recall skill to check for relevant portfolio decisions; the supplied brief remains the source of truth.The composition is now set: the work index comes before the image on mobile, the RAG project gets a full-width dark experiment spread, Application Copilot reads as an inspection sheet, and TypeForge becomes a typographic study. The memory search returned no matching portfolio decisions.\nThe full homepage is ready to inspect. The three projects now have distinct compositions, and the TypeForge key provides a small, working case-change interaction.\n\nI’m checking the factual copy, narrow-screen fit and keyboard states, then preparing the desktop and mobile renders.I’ll audit the concept against the supplied brief, focusing on content accuracy, accessible navigation and narrow-screen layout risks. This is a read-only review; rendered layout remains the lead’s verification step.Read-only review found four concrete issues:\n\n- **P1: Invisible key focus ring.** `the-working-table.html:38,138` uses `currentColor` for focus outlines, while the key’s foreground and surrounding section are both `--surface`. Add `.type-key:focus-visible { outline-color: var(--fg); }`.\n- **P2: Some desktop body copy is below the requested 16px minimum.** Inspection-flow paragraphs are 15px (`:125`), qualification copy 14px (`:128`), and TypeForge descriptions 15px (`:148`). These contain substantive project information.\n- **P2: Tablet diagram labels become very small.** At 768px, the 1200-unit desktop diagram renders approximately 700px wide: 16px labels shrink to 9.3px. The vertical diagram only activates below 768px (`:214-215`). Consider switching diagrams below 1024px.\n- **P2: Compact navigation lacks full 44px touch targets.** Links have 44px height but no minimum width (`:57,193`); the wordmark has neither minimum dimension (`:55,191`). `min-width:44px` on navigation links and `min-height:44px` on the wordmark should fit the current mobile arrangement.\n\nStatic checks passed: unique IDs, valid internal link targets, valid `aria-labelledby` references, existing local image, and all five requested real links. Project order, benchmark conditions/setup, Copilot qualification limits, TypeForge claims and illustration provenance match the brief.\n\nFont-metric checks indicate the 390px name fits narrowly; at 320px it extends about 4px into the right gutter, without reaching the viewport edge. This is a render-check watch point, not confirmed horizontal overflow.\n\nNo files changed. Browser rendering and interaction execution were intentionally outside this review slice.",
